title: Phased idempotency & retry contract for buffered-generate -> unified-generate migration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define the API contract, server-side behavior, SDK guidance and rollout gates for preserving safe retry and dedup semantics while retiring the legacy buffered-generate behavior in favor of the unified/generate endpoint. This ticket covers the PRD-level migration requirements, acceptance criteria, and staged rollout plan focused on idempotency keys, replay windows, status semantics and observable signals for customers and internal ops.
background: Historically the legacy buffered-generate endpoints allowed clients to POST payloads without consistent idempotency guarantees; retries by clients could cause duplicate work or partial duplicate outputs. The unified/generate endpoint provides stronger lifecycle primitives but requires a clear migration contract so existing customers do not observe doubled outputs, billing surprises, or broken at-least-once semantics during phased cutovers. We must specify: server semantics for Idempotency-Key, how long replay history is retained, expected response codes for repeated submissions, SDK changes, and telemetry gates to ensure safe rollback.
migration_steps: Finalize server-side idempotency design: accept optional Idempotency-Key header and dedupe requests within a configurable window (default 48h), return consistent operation_id and canonical response for duplicates.
Implement backward-compat shim: for 60-day compatibility window map legacy buffered-generate client request IDs to new idempotency keys for tenants with migration mode enabled.
SDK updates: add optional idempotency_key parameter to Python/JS/Go SDKs; default to client-generated UUIDs for long-running operations; surface operation replay errors with clear retry guidance.
Docs & migration guide: publish migration doc with code examples, recommended idempotency key patterns, and a checklist for customers (when to set, when to avoid).
Internal tooling: add replay-log retention dashboard, dedupe hit-rate metric, and a 'replay-duplicates' alert to Redwood Console.
Canary rollout: enable strict-idempotency mode for 5% of requests for 1 week with telemetry gates; expand to 50% then 100% following gating criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Server honors Idempotency-Key header for POST /v1/generate: duplicate requests within 48 hours return identical response payload and do not double-bill beyond the original token accounting (billing exceptions documented).
If Idempotency-Key is absent, server behavior remains best-effort: unified/generate must document non-idempotent semantics and recommend client-side keys.
For mapped legacy requests (compat shim), responses must match legacy buffered payload shape or include a compatibility wrapper that SDKs can unwrap without content drift.
SDKs (Python/JS/Go) release: idempotency_key param + examples, migration guide included in changelog, and integration tests verifying dedupe behavior against a test sandbox.
Telemetry: dedupe-hit-rate, duplicate-billing-incidents, and idempotency-key-adoption-rates are instrumented and visible in Console; gating alerts configured.
Rollout gates: no more than 0.5% of migrated requests observed as unexpected duplicates causing customer-facing regressions during each expansion step.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (prep): complete server APIs, SDK changes, docs and internal dashboards. (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (canary): enable dedupe for 5% of tenant traffic and run smoke tests; monitor dedupe-hit-rate and billing deltas. (1 week)
Phase 2 (gradual expansion): 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 3 weeks with automated rollback if gate thresholds exceeded.
Phase 3 (compat window): enable mapping shim for legacy-flagged tenants for 60 days; proactively contact top-200 customers to opt into migration assistance.
Phase 4 (cutover): remove legacy buffered-generate endpoints and finalize canonical unified/generate contract after compatibility window ends.
telemetry_and_gating: Primary gates: dedupe-hit-rate, duplicate-output-incidents, idempotency-key-adoption-rate (per-tenant), and billing-delta-per-tenant.
Gate thresholds: fail fast if duplicate-output-incidents > 0.5% of requests in canary, or if billing-delta > 2% for any tenant in a 24h window.
Dashboards: per-tenant idempotency key adoption, dedupe latency (time to detect duplicate), and operation_id resolution success rate.
Audit logs: persist mapping events (legacy-id -> idempotency-key) with tenant id and timestamp for 180 days (security team signoff required).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Clients using non-deterministic prompts may expect different outputs on retry; deduplication could hide legitimate retries. Mitigation: document guidance and add opt-out header for clients that prefer at-least-once semantics.
Risk: Billing discrepancies when dedupe mask cost; mitigation: produce per-request billing metadata and a reconciliation job for impacted tenants; notify affected customers during canary phase.
Risk: Increased storage for replay logs. Mitigation: default 48h retention with configurable tiers and cleanup job; allow enterprise tenants to opt into longer windows.
Risk: SDK rollout bugs causing malformed idempotency keys. Mitigation: integration test suite, canary SDK release channel, and client-side validation in SDKs.

2025-02-09 | Diego Moreno: Spoke with Runtime leads. Kernel-level dedupe is possible but adds ~8% latency at tail in worst-case; recommend implementing dedupe at routing+cache layer for first pass. Raised implementation trade-offs in GH PR linked.
2025-02-09 | Sasha Ivanov (Engineering): Suggested making dedupe window configurable per-tenant to mitigate storage overhead for enterprise customers. Will prototype TTL-based metadata store.
2025-02-10 | Priya Nair (Design): UX note: SDK error messages should surface 'idempotency-duplicate' with a link to the migration guide. We'll provide copy for SDK changelogs.

2025-02-10 | Diego Moreno: Updated rollout schedule to include a 60-day compatibility window for legacy mapping and confirmed gate thresholds. Next: finalize SDK API surface and schedule SDK canary release.
